**Finding: deviation (Section 10.3, ¶p0063) — redline validated and submitted.**

- **What the document says:** Section 10.3 is a bare "binding upon successors and assigns" provision. It contains no consent standard, no competitor bar, and no assignment restriction on either side.
- **Direction check:** Our own assignment freedom is unimpaired (no prohibition, no M&A carve-out needed), and I confirmed there is no change-of-control trigger anywhere — searches for "change of control" and "merger" return nothing, and the only termination rights are the Company's 70-day launch right (¶p0011) and the mutual 90-day notice right (¶p0024). So this is not walk-away territory.
- **Why it still fails:** The fallback requires consent for non-successor assignments not to be unreasonably withheld. Here HDI can assign the whole Agreement — including to one of our competitors — without notice or consent. That vendor-side control is a material term and is entirely absent, so the clause sits below the fallback.
- **Redline (preferred position, minimal insert to 10.3):** HDI may not assign without our prior written consent (not unreasonably withheld or delayed) and never to a competitor; the Company may assign to an affiliate or successor by merger/asset sale without HDI's consent; and no change of control of the Company gives HDI a termination, re-pricing or suspension right. The comment offers the mutual notice-based fallback if HDI pushes back.
